questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Semiconductor Diodes, Zener Diodes & Diode Circuits (Rectifiers, Clippers, Clampers)
questions.text: Explain the PN junction diode operation under forward and reverse bias with energy band diagrams and Shockley's Diode Equation: $I = I_s (e^{V_D / \eta V_T} - 1)$. Explain Dynamic Resistance ($r_d = \frac{\eta V_T}{I_D}$) and Transition/Diffusion capacitances.

questions.chapter: Chapter 6: Feedback Amplifiers & Sinusoidal Oscillators (Barkhausen Criterion, Wien Bridge, Colpitts)
questions.text: Explain Full-Wave Bridge Rectifier with a capacitor filter. Derive Ripple Factor ($r = \frac{1}{4\sqrt{3} f C R_L}$), DC load voltage ($V_{dc} = V_m - \frac{I_{dc}}{4 f C}$), and Peak Inverse Voltage ($PIV = V_m$).

questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Semiconductor Diodes, Zener Diodes & Diode Circuits (Rectifiers, Clippers, Clampers)
questions.text: Explain Diode Clipper (Limiter) and Clamper (DC Restorer) circuits. Draw output voltage waveforms for positive and negative biased clippers and clampers with a sinusoidal input $v_{in}(t) = 15\sin(\omega t)\,\text{V}$.

questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Semiconductor Diodes, Zener Diodes & Diode Circuits (Rectifiers, Clippers, Clampers)
questions.text: Explain Zener Diode voltage regulation. A $10\,\text{V}$ Zener diode has maximum power rating $P_{z,max} = 500\,\text{mW}$ and knee current $I_{zk} = 5\,\text{mA}$. Design the series current limiting resistor $R_s$ to maintain $10\,\text{V}$ across load $R_L$ with input varying from $15\,\text{V}$ to $25\,\text{V}$ and load current varying from $5\,\text{mA}$ to $35\,\text{mA}$.

questions.chapter: Chapter 3: Field Effect Transistors (JFET & MOSFET Characteristics, Biasing & Amplifiers)
questions.text: Explain Common Emitter (CE) configuration of BJT. Draw input and output characteristics, and define Cutoff, Active, and Saturation regions. Explain Early Effect (Base-Width Modulation) and Early Voltage ($V_A$).

questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Semiconductor Diodes, Zener Diodes & Diode Circuits (Rectifiers, Clippers, Clampers)
questions.text: Explain BJT Biasing circuits: Fixed Bias, Collector-to-Base Feedback Bias, and Voltage Divider Bias (Self-Bias). Derive the Stability Factor $S(I_{co}) = \frac{1 + \beta}{1 + \beta \frac{R_e}{R_e + R_{th}}}$ and show that Voltage Divider Bias provides the most stable Q-point.

questions.chapter: Chapter 2: Bipolar Junction Transistors (BJT Characteristics, Biasing & Small-Signal AC Models)
questions.text: Draw the Small-Signal $re$-model and hybrid-$h$ parameter model for a CE amplifier with unbypassed emitter resistor $R_E$. Derive expressions for Input Impedance ($Z_i$), Output Impedance ($Z_o$), Voltage Gain ($A_v = -\frac{R_c}{r_e + R_E}$), and Current Gain ($A_i$).

questions.chapter: Chapter 3: Field Effect Transistors (JFET & MOSFET Characteristics, Biasing & Amplifiers)
questions.text: Explain the construction and operation of N-channel Junction Field Effect Transistor (JFET). Explain Pinch-Off Voltage ($V_p$) and derive Shockley's Equation: $I_D = I_{DSS}\left(1 - \frac{V_{GS}}{V_p}\right)^2$. Define Transconductance $g_m = g_{m0}\left(1 - \frac{V_{GS}}{V_p}\right)$ where $g_{m0} = \frac{2I_{DSS}}{|V_p|}$.

questions.chapter: Chapter 3: Field Effect Transistors (JFET & MOSFET Characteristics, Biasing & Amplifiers)
questions.text: Compare Enhancement MOSFET (E-MOSFET) vs Depletion MOSFET (D-MOSFET). Explain CMOS Inverter operation, voltage transfer curve (VTC), and explain why static power dissipation in CMOS is virtually zero.

questions.chapter: Chapter 5: Operational Amplifiers (Op-Amps, Inverting/Non-Inverting, Integrators, Differentiators)
questions.text: Explain Ideal Op-Amp characteristics ($A_{OL} = \infty, R_{in} = \infty, R_{out} = 0, \text{CMRR} = \infty, BW = \infty$) and Virtual Ground concept. Derive the closed-loop voltage gain for: (a) Inverting Amplifier ($A_v = -R_f/R_1$), (b) Non-Inverting Amplifier ($A_v = 1 + R_f/R_1$), and (c) Inverting Summing Amplifier.

questions.chapter: Chapter 5: Operational Amplifiers (Op-Amps, Inverting/Non-Inverting, Integrators, Differentiators)
questions.text: Explain Instrumentation Amplifier using 3 Op-Amps. Derive the differential voltage gain: $A_d = \left(1 + \frac{2R_1}{R_{gain}}\right)\frac{R_3}{R_2}$. Why is an instrumentation amplifier widely used in biomedical and sensor measurement systems?

questions.chapter: Chapter 6: Feedback Amplifiers & Sinusoidal Oscillators (Barkhausen Criterion, Wien Bridge, Colpitts)
questions.text: Explain Negative Feedback topologies: Voltage-Series, Voltage-Shunt, Current-Series, and Current-Shunt. Prove that negative feedback stabilizes voltage gain ($A_f = \frac{A}{1 + A\beta}$), reduces distortion, and increases bandwidth ($BW_f = BW(1 + A\beta)$).

questions.chapter: Chapter 6: Feedback Amplifiers & Sinusoidal Oscillators (Barkhausen Criterion, Wien Bridge, Colpitts)
questions.text: State Barkhausen's Criterion for sustained sinusoidal oscillations ($|A\beta| = 1, \angle A\beta = 0^\circ$ or $360^\circ$). Explain RC Phase Shift Oscillator (Derive $f_0 = \frac{1}{2\pi R C \sqrt{6}}$ and $h_{fe} \ge 29$) and Wien Bridge Oscillator ($f_0 = \frac{1}{2\pi R C}, A_v \ge 3$).

questions.chapter: Chapter 3: Field Effect Transistors (JFET & MOSFET Characteristics, Biasing & Amplifiers)
questions.text: Classify Power Amplifiers: Class A ($\eta_{max} = 25\%$ or $50\%$), Class B ($\eta_{max} = 78.5\%$), Class AB, and Class C. Explain Cross-Over Distortion in Class B push-pull amplifiers and how Class AB complementary symmetry solves it.

questions.chapter: Chapter 4: Frequency Response of BJT and FET Amplifiers (Low/High Frequency Cutoff, Bode Plots)
questions.text: Derive output equations for Op-Amp Differentiator and Op-Amp Integrator ($v_o(t) = -\frac{1}{RC}\int v_{in}(t)dt$). Explain practical integrator and practical differentiator with parallel feedback resistor $R_f$ and series input resistor $R_s$ to overcome high-frequency and low-frequency instability.
